findings.failing_input: Hook mounts after a write has already fired. The mount-time setOneTime(readOneTime()) seeds from localStorage; the event listener registers AFTER. A second write that happens BEFORE this useEffect runs (impossible due to React's sync useEffect) would be missed.
findings.expected: Standard React lifecycle: useEffect runs after mount, listener attached.

findings.failing_input: Two writes fire in rapid succession from the same hook instance: persist(A) → safeWrite dispatches 'roas-billing-changed' (listener sees selfWritePending=true, sets to false). Now another component fires writeOneTime(B) → event dispatched. selfWritePending is already false, listener re-reads. Correct.
findings.expected: Cross-hook re-reads should not be suppressed.
findings.actual: Correct. The ref flips at first event and remains false until next persist() call. Cross-component writes are caught.
findings.regression_test_idea: Pin: persist(A) followed by another component's writeOneTime(B) — assert this hook's state ends up = B.

findings.failing_input: persist(next) sets local state synchronously THEN flips ref THEN calls writeOneTime which fires event. Listener observes the ref AS-IS (true), clears it, skips re-read.
findings.actual: Correct. The ref-flip happens between setOneTime and writeOneTime. The event dispatch from writeOneTime is synchronous, so the listener runs on the same call stack — sees ref=true, clears it.
findings.regression_test_idea: Unit test: spy on setOneTime, assert called once per persist(); assert no extra re-read on the listener path.
